title: strictConcaveOn_of_deriv2_neg: The Calculus Criterion in Lean 4
content: The proof applies Mathlib's strictConcaveOn_of_deriv2_neg (from Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Deriv): given a convex domain D, ContinuousOn f D, and deriv^[2] f x < 0 for all x ∈ interior D, conclude StrictConcaveOn ℝ D f. The signature uses deriv^[2] (the iterated Fréchet derivative as a function ℝ → ℝ) rather than HasDerivAt, which requires care: deriv^[2] f x is only equal to the second derivative when the function is indeed differentiable — which must be established separately via EventuallyEq.deriv_eq. The convex domain is convex_Ioo 0 1, and the interior equals itself since Ioo is already open: interior_Ioo is used to simplify. This is the standard way to prove strict concavity in Lean 4 for smooth functions on open intervals.
mathContext: $h(p) = -p\log p - (1-p)\log(1-p)$. Criterion: if $h$ is $C^2$ and $h''(p) < 0$ on $(0,1)$, then $h$ is strictly concave. Standard calculus: $h'(p) = \log(1-p) - \log p$, $h''(p) = -\frac{1}{1-p} - \frac{1}{p} < 0$ for $p \in (0,1)$.

title: First Derivative: Product Rule + Chain Rule for -p·log(p) - (1-p)·log(1-p)
content: The lemma h_hasDerivAt computes h'(p) = log(1-p) - log(p) in two sub-computations. For x·log(x): (hasDerivAt_id p).mul (Real.hasDerivAt_log (ne_of_gt hp0)) gives HasDerivAt (x·log(x)) (1·log(p) + p·(1/p)) p. The simplification 1·log(p) = log(p) uses simp only [id, one_mul], and p·(1/p) = 1 uses rwa [mul_inv_cancel₀ (ne_of_gt hp0)]. For (1-x)·log(1-x): compose the y·log(y) derivative with the derivative of 1-x (HasDerivAt (1-x) (-1) p, proved by simpa [id, zero_sub] from (hasDerivAt_const p 1).sub (hasDerivAt_id p)), then apply hd_at.comp p hd_sub and convert using ring. The final line `convert (hd_xlogx.add hd_1xlog1x).neg using 1; ring` adds the two sub-derivatives and negates, converting the type to match h.
mathContext: $\frac{d}{dp}[p\log p] = \log p + 1$, $\frac{d}{dp}[(1-p)\log(1-p)] = (-1)(\log(1-p)+1) = -\log(1-p)-1$. Sum: $\frac{d}{dp}[p\log p + (1-p)\log(1-p)] = \log p - \log(1-p)$. Negating gives $h'(p) = \log(1-p) - \log p$.

title: EventuallyEq.deriv_eq: Chaining HasDerivAt Lemmas for deriv^[2]
content: The main theorem h_strictConcaveOn needs to show deriv^[2] h x < 0. The challenge: deriv^[2] = deriv (deriv h), and `deriv h` is defined as a limit which doesn't directly simplify. The solution uses EventuallyEq.deriv_eq: if f =ᶠ[𝓝 x] g (equal as functions in a neighborhood), then deriv f x = deriv g x. The proof constructs heq : deriv h =ᶠ[𝓝 x] (fun y => log(1-y) - log y) by applying Filter.eventually_of_mem with Ioo_mem_nhds hx0 hx1 (the neighborhood around x intersects Ioo 0 1) and using (h_hasDerivAt y hy.1 hy.2).deriv at each point. Then rw [EventuallyEq.deriv_eq heq] replaces deriv (deriv h) with deriv (log(1-y)-log(y)), and (h_hasDerivAt2 x hx0 hx1).deriv gives the explicit value. This two-step approach — HasDerivAt for explicit values, EventuallyEq for deriv equality — is idiomatic in Mathlib when the target function is defined only implicitly.
mathContext: The key Lean 4 chain: $\text{deriv}^{[2]} h(x) = \text{deriv}(\text{deriv} h)(x) \overset{\text{eq.}}{=} \text{deriv}(\log(1-\cdot) - \log)(x) \overset{\text{HasDeriv}}{=} -\frac{1}{1-x} - \frac{1}{x}$. The EventuallyEq bridges the implicit `deriv h` to the explicit formula.
prerequisites: Ioo_mem_nhds for nhds in open intervals
HasDerivAt.deriv: HasDerivAt f f' x → deriv f x = f'

title: h''(p) < 0: Ring Rewrite + add_pos + linarith
content: The lemma h_deriv2_neg proves -1/(1-p) - 1/p < 0 for p ∈ (0,1) in four lines. The critical step is heq: rewrite -1/(1-p) - 1/p = -(1/(1-p) + 1/p) via ring. This is necessary because linarith cannot directly combine the atoms -1/(1-p), -1/p, and 0 — it needs them as negations of positive quantities. After the ring rewrite, h1 : 0 < 1/(1-p) and h2 : 0 < 1/p from div_pos one_pos, then linarith [add_pos h1 h2] concludes -(1/(1-p) + 1/p) < 0. This ring-first-then-linarith pattern is standard in Lean 4 analysis when arithmetic involves fractions that linarith cannot handle directly.
prerequisites: div_pos for positive divisor and dividend
linarith for linear arithmetic over ordered fields

title: ContinuousOn h: Composition of Continuity Lemmas
content: The continuity proof for h on (0,1) unfolds h and applies ContinuousOn.neg, ContinuousOn.add, and ContinuousOn.mul in sequence. For x·log(x): continuousOn_id.mul (continuousOn_id.log (fun x hx => ne_of_gt hx.1)) — the nonvanishing condition for log requires x ≠ 0, provided by hx.1 (x ∈ Ioo 0 1 means 0 < x). For (1-x)·log(1-x): (continuousOn_const.sub continuousOn_id).mul (...).log (fun x hx => ne_of_gt (by simp only [id_eq]; linarith [hx.2])) — the nonvanishing condition for log(1-x) requires 1-x ≠ 0, i.e., x ≠ 1, proved by simp only [id_eq] to simplify the id and then linarith from hx.2 (x < 1). The simp only [id_eq] is needed because the expression involves id applied to x, which doesn't automatically reduce.
mathContext: $h(p) = -(p \log p + (1-p)\log(1-p))$ is continuous on $(0,1)$: each term is a product of continuous functions, and $\log$ is continuous away from 0.
